checks: Each injected open/Snapshot/Transition storage failure starts from a successfully created real temporary-file journal, avoiding rejection of an invalid initial fixture as a false fault-path pass.
Create faults use an initially empty regular file; directory/nonempty/invalid-handle rejection is tested separately.
Read injection is one-shot and short-read injection resets its byte counter on SeekStart. It distinguishes actual read failure/early EOF from frame corruption.

Read/write/seek/stat/Sync/lock/unlock failures expect fixed integrity errors and shared poison where required; invalid inputs and deliberate nil journal internals do not falsely assert persistence failure.
Unlock or Sync failure after a complete write does not assert that no frame exists. This preserves the SDD's uncertain outcome and complete-frame recovery semantics.
Map-ordered subtests use independent files, locks and health domains and are not parallelized; no outcome dependence on their iteration order was found.
The beforeGate poison callback is a synchronous fault seam for the post-lock guard, not evidence of an additional real concurrent schedule. Existing dedicated concurrency tests remain separate.
nonblocking_limitations: The generic Transition stat/seek injections fail during initial replay; they do not specifically prove the later second Stat or append SeekEnd failure paths. Do not attribute those exact branches to these tests without coverage evidence.
New fault tests primarily assert returned category and poison; they do not independently count every I/O stage or establish full supervisor zero-side-effect authorization.
Earlier notes about in-process barrier timeout coverage and incomplete forced-child termination remain unchanged.
